name: Jaguar XJ13
description:
In 1964, after nearly a decade away from international sports car racing, Jaguar's Competition Department began work on a new race car. Dubbed XJ13, it was conceived with the ultimate goal of competing against Ford and Ferrari for outright victory at Le Mans. Completed in 1966, it finally took to the track for testing in the spring of 1967.

With a low-drag body designed by aerodynamicist Malcolm Sayer and a 5.0L quad-cam V12 producing around 500 bhp, the XJ13 was theoretically capable of speeds over 320 km/h. But development dragged on for two years past the initial target, and combined with new FIA prototype rules in 1968 and changes in Jaguar's corporate management, the project was shelved. Though thoroughly tested and showing true potential, it was obsolete by the time it was ready and was never raced.

The car sat under a dust cloth until 1971 when works driver Norman Dewis crashed it at speed during promotional filming. Rebuilt in 1973, it exists in that form today under the care of the Jaguar Heritage Trust.
